## PM grading — the choice here is a **privacy decision**, not an engineering one. Routing to the maintainer.

PM dispatch seat, session `session_01Y26DJEHSBhhAQ6wwfsHNza`. `domain:identity` is this seat's lane, so I would normally rule and dispatch. ⛔ I am not, and the reason is which of the two options is cheap.

### What is measured

`sys_audit_log`'s **`record_views`** list view declares an `ip_address` column. `buildRow` in `read-audit.ts` stamps `action` / `created_at` / `user_id` / `object_name` / `record_id` / `old_value` / `new_value` / `tenant_id` (plus conditional `organization_id` and `actor`) and **never `ip_address`**. ⇒ The last column of the shipped *"who viewed this record"* view is **empty on every row it can ever show.**

⚠️ **Why this is worse than an ordinary declared-but-unwritten column.** On this screen the blank does not read as "not captured" — it reads as **"we captured the fingerprint and there was none."** An auditor looking at a compliance view interprets an empty cell as evidence about the event, not as evidence about the schema. That is the same untruthful-by-omission shape as #9517, one layer down, and on the surface we just shipped for a regulated-industry buyer.

Correctly identified as the same defect class as the **#7675 / #8147 / #8315** enum retirements on this exact object — a declared **column** with no writer, rather than a declared **value** with no writer.

### Why I am not ruling it

The two options are **not** symmetric:

- **Drop the column** — honest, cheap, no new data. Says "we do not capture viewer IP."
- **Stamp it** — capturing the **viewer's IP address on every record view** is a new class of personal data collected on a hot path, retained under the audit object's retention policy, and visible to anyone who can read the audit view. ⚠️ In the GDPR-adjacent market this feature was built for, that is a **privacy posture decision** with its own compliance consequences — plausibly the opposite of the ones it looks like it serves.

⇒ An engineering seat can implement either. ⛔ Neither this seat nor a dev should **choose**, because the choice is about what personal data the platform collects by default.

**My recommendation, recorded not taken: drop the column.** It is reversible (adding it later is additive), it makes the shipped view honest immediately, and nothing measured says a buyer asked for viewer-IP capture — the bank RFI behind #8992 asked for *who viewed which record*, which `user_id` already answers. ⚠️ If the answer is instead "stamp it", that wants its own card with a retention and access decision attached, ⛔ not a one-line addition to `buildRow`.

### Coupling to note

PR #9541 (#9517's residual) documents this empty column deliberately, per the ruling there — ⛔ staying silent about it would have been the untruthful-narrow failure. **If this card lands as "drop the column", the taker also deletes that one README bullet**, which is named in this card's body and asserted by nothing, so nothing goes red either way.

Labelled `needs-user-decision`. ⛔ Left unassigned.

Maintainer ruling (2026-08-18, live PM chat with the triage seat, session `session_01EUZUjvnLsqwHVkXkTv8TKQ`; verbatim: 「其他接受你的建议」, applying the triage recommendation delivered for this card).

**Ruled: Option 1.** Drop `ip_address` from the `record_views` view's columns and replace it with `actor` (the column the read writer does stamp, and the one that attributes a service principal). Rationale of record: the narrow-not-untruthful audit-surface principle (#7675/#8147/#8315 class); an always-blank fingerprint column on a compliance view is a wrong positive claim. The stamp-it capability (Option 2) is explicitly NOT commissioned — if it is ever wanted it is a separate Feature card, mindful that the read writer is allocation-only on the request path.

Returned to `pm:queue`, type Bug (a declared column no writer ever writes = declared≠enforced). Dispatch note: fix is one column-list edit in `sys-audit-log.object.ts` + a pin that the `record_views` columns ⊆ the read-writer's stamped key set, so the class can't regrow.

Triage auto-adjudication (bug-repair lane; confidence gate checked — all four facets point the same way, not on the human floor, no prior ruling narrowed or reversed). Duplicate #9865 (closed → here) independently confirmed the measurement and added: the docs page (PR #9860) positively states "No IP address and no user agent", so screen and docs currently disagree.

<!-- os-decision-facets -->
- **platform long-term coherence**: 审计面宁窄勿谎 is the already-stated principle of #7675/#8147/#8315 on this same object — dropping the unwritable column is the fourth application, one layer down (column instead of enum value).
- **measured business pull**: zero — no writer stamps `ip_address` on `read` rows and none can (`ReadAuditEvent` carries no field for it); the measured cost is an evaluator reading a false capability claim off the shipped compliance screen.
- **AI-agent error-resistance**: a column that is declaratively present but structurally unwritable is exactly the declared≠enforced shape; removing it restores declared = enforced. Stamping instead would widen the read hot path against #8992's deliberate MVP scope pins.
- **startup scope discipline**: remove beats declare-and-maintain; viewer-IP capture, if ever wanted, is a product decision to make on its own pull (option 2 stays available as a future card).

**Ruling (auto-adjudicated): option 1** — drop `ip_address` from the `record_views` view columns in `sys-audit-log.object.ts`; the filer's suggested replacement column `actor` (which the read writer DOES stamp and which attributes service principals) is a good same-line improvement, dev's call. Keep the docs page (PR #9860 wording) as-is — it becomes correct by construction.

**Confidence gap**: this analysis assumes viewer IP is not a compliance requirement anyone has committed to; if the maintainer wants IP-on-views as a capability, veto this and it becomes option 2 (a scope-widening decision card). Veto window: this ruling executes via normal dispatch, not immediately.

**Fork-back clause**: if implementation finds the contract must move anyway (e.g. the view schema rejects the column removal somewhere), stop and return this card to `needs-user-decision`.
